executive_summary: Recent advisories highlight critical vulnerabilities in enterprise software (Plex, Fortinet, Atlassian) and Python libraries (filelock, virtualenv). Key trends include command injection, SSRF, path traversal, and insecure temporary file handling. These require immediate patching and secure coding practices.

signals.title: Plex Media Server SSRF and Path Traversal Chain (CVE-2026-96652, 96654, 96655, 96656)
signals.what_changed: Multiple SSRF and path traversal flaws in Plex allow authenticated users to write arbitrary files and execute code via chained exploits.
signals.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how attackers combine vulnerabilities to escalate privileges and compromise systems.
signals.application: Build a lab simulating SSRF/path traversal in a web app; implement input validation and sandboxing.

signals.title: Atlassian Arbitrary File Access (CVE-2026-21589)
signals.what_changed: Unauthenticated attackers can access files in web app root directories across multiple Atlassian products.
signals.why_it_matters: Exposes sensitive data and enables further exploitation in enterprise environments.
signals.application: Audit file access controls in web apps; use chroot jails or containerization to restrict paths.

signals.title: Ahsay CBS Command Injection and Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-105133, 105134)
signals.what_changed: Command injection and authentication bypass in Ahsay CBS allow remote code execution.
signals.why_it_matters: Highlights risks of unsanitized input and weak authentication in API endpoints.
signals.application: Practice input sanitization and secure API design in Python/Flask apps.

signals.title: filelock Race Condition (GHSA-jqc4-5cvw-7w85)
signals.what_changed: Race condition in filelock allows deletion of arbitrary directories via hard-link manipulation.
signals.why_it_matters: Demonstrates insecure temporary file handling in Python libraries.
signals.application: Implement atomic file operations and use secure temporary directories in Python projects.

signals.title: Fortinet Path Traversal (CVE-2025-61624)
signals.what_changed: Authenticated path traversal in Fortinet products allows arbitrary file write/delete.
signals.why_it_matters: Enables system compromise via CLI command manipulation in network devices.
signals.application: Test path traversal mitigations in CLI tools; enforce strict input validation.

experiment.title: SSRF and Path Traversal Mitigation Lab
experiment.objective: Simulate and mitigate SSRF/path traversal vulnerabilities in a controlled web app.
prerequisites: OWASP WebGoat or custom Flask app
steps: Deploy a vulnerable Flask app with SSRF and path traversal endpoints.
Use curl/Burp to exploit SSRF to access internal services.
Exploit path traversal to read/write files outside the web root.
Implement input validation, URL allowlists, and sandboxing.
expected_evidence: Successful SSRF/path traversal exploitation in the lab.
Logs showing blocked attempts and sanitized inputs.
experiment.stop_condition: All exploitation attempts are blocked by mitigations.

discarded: Low-severity GitHub advisories (virtualenv, filelock oplock) and non-chained vulnerabilities with limited practical impact for portfolio projects.
backlog: Monitor CISA KEV updates for new entries.
Explore cloud-specific vulnerabilities in AWS/Azure IAM misconfigurations.
Investigate AI/ML model poisoning as a defensive threat vector.
